detail: Canonical policy attempt: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin LLVM=1 LLVM_IAS=1 CROSS_COMPILE= CC=/usr/bin/clang LD=/usr/bin/ld AR=/usr/bin/llvm-ar NM=/usr/bin/llvm-nm OBJCOPY=/usr/bin/llvm-objcopy OBJDUMP=/usr/bin/llvm-objdump READELF=/usr/bin/llvm-readelf STRIP=/usr/bin/llvm-strip HOSTCC=/usr/bin/clang HOSTCXX=/usr/bin/clang++ HOSTLD=/usr/bin/ld make -C vendor/linux O=rewrite/kbuild/{x86_64,aarch64} ARCH={x86_64,arm64} SRCARCH={x86,arm64} KBUILD_HOSTLDFLAGS=-fuse-ld=bfd defconfig. Both invocations exited 2. stderr: scripts/Kconfig.include:41: linker 'ld.lld' not found. Kbuild's LLVM=1 configuration probing requires ld.lld even when GNU ld is explicitly supplied; no matching LLVM ld.lld is installed. The PATH-selected /home/fenhir/.local/bin/ld.lld is Rust LLD 22.1.6, while clang/LLVM tools are Debian LLVM 19.1.7, so it cannot be accepted as the canonical linker.
required_resolution: Install or otherwise provide a pinned LLVM 19.1.7 ld.lld for both architectures, then rerun configuration stabilization and metadata extraction from clean outputs. Do not use the Rust LLD 22 path or mix GCC-generated configs with LLVM metadata. Keep this blocker until both defconfig invocations and second synchronization passes succeed.
